Impacts oftheFrench Revolution
The French Revolution is one of the most important events in the world history as it had
long-lasting impacts on Europe and the world.The long-term impacts shaped politics,
society, religion and ideas in France and worldwide.
The French Revolution encouraged the separation of the religion and the affairs of
the state (Secularism).
It weakened the absolute monarchismin France,as the King was then bound bythe
constitution.
It led to the founding of new republics and liberal democracies across Europe and
across the Atlantic.
It became an example for several independence movements and national
revolutions in various countries worldwide.
The socially-discriminative estate system was abolished as the nobility held no
additional rights on the poor farmers in France.
The Church of France lost its dictating power on the lives and properties of its
followers.
Slavery was abolished in French colonies, and it led to the Haiti Revolution across
the Atlantic between 1791and1804.
Economic equality was one of the fruits of the French Revolution. Lands earlier
owned by the Church and the nobility were distributed to small landowners.
Several ideological alternatives surfaced due to the French Revolution including
nationalism,liberalism,socialismandcommunism.
The French Revolution had a deep impact on neighbouring countries like Belgium,
nobility and clergy just like it happened in.France.
